params.body:
## The remaining voting routes act only on the dealer's own cars

Follow-up to #1052, from the October architecture audit (#1047). #1052 closed the seller rating; the
other voting routes behind the login still took the record id straight from the URL (base64, so
guessable) and acted on whatever car or bidding it named. The `Access` middleware guards the verb,
not whose car it is.

- **Buyer rating** (`addBuyerVote`/`storeBuyerVote`) — the seller rates the buyer of a car it sold.
  The GET modal now requires the sold car to be the dealer's own (`mustOwnVehicle`); the POST requires
  the logged-in dealer to be the seller of the buyer's copy (`seller_id`). Before, a dealer could
  save a buyer rating on another garage's deal, written as if from that garage.
- **Export buyer rating** (`addExportBuyerVote`/`storeExportBuyerVote`) — the selling dealer rates the
  winning bidder. Both now require the bidding's car to be the dealer's own (`mustOwnExport` on the
  GET, before the pickup-release check; a 403 on the POST before it marks the bidding delivered).
- **Set winner** (`setWinner`) — the heaviest: it writes `bidding_winner` (irreversible, R B1-5.4)
  and mails every bidder (R B1-5.5). It now refuses a bidding that is not the dealer's own, so a
  logged-in dealer can no longer pick the winner of someone else's auction.

The no-login route where the winner rates the seller (R B1-5.11) stays public on purpose: the emailed
link is itself the capability, the winner has no account. It already aborts cleanly on a bad id.

Ownership is read from `export_vehicle->vehicle->dealer_id` (the selling dealer) for the bidding
routes, and from the vehicle's `dealer_id`/`seller_id` for the buy-over routes, matching the idiom
the rest of the app uses.

### Still open (named, not in this PR)

From the same audit: the read routes `StockListController::getRelationData` and
`VehicleTextController::generate`, the `ExportController` PDFs, and the broad filter-key allowlist in
`VehicleRepository::extendedSearch`.

### Tests

`VoteRoutesCheckOwnershipTest`: each route refuses a stranger dealer (403) and leaves the rating or
the winner untouched; the selling dealer may still rate the buyer and set the winner; the no-login
dealer vote stays open without a login. The four refusal cases fail on main; the three own/open cases
already pass. `RatingScreenTest` (the happy-path rating screens) stays green unchanged.

Rules R S5-3.12, R B1-5.4 and R B1-5.8 carry the ownership; R B1-5.11 notes it is deliberately public.
PHPStan clean; full suite green.
params.title: The remaining voting routes act only on the dealer's own cars
